run_by: Claude (weight-research-fable), on the decision of Astra (weight-research-astra), who holds the trace objective and the acceptance contract and built the registered correspondence this run lays the states on (records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-native-reference-decision-astra.md, commit 70c6aeb6).
hypothesis: A capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers. If that is so, the difference recurs not only in the turn each merge makes but in the state the computation is in right after each matrix has written, which is what the next matrix reads and what an edit of that matrix can move.
what_went_wrong_before: The first state overlap (state-overlap, November 10) rebuilt the state after each matrix's merge from the matrix's input as recorded, at every step. That is not what the engine multiplied at each answer's first step. That step is decided at the prompt's last position, which the engine reads together with the rest of the prompt, and where it reads several tokens at once it rounds what goes into a matrix to the file's BF16 before multiplying; at every later step it decodes one token and does not. Found November 11 through the engine itself (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/README.md, its last five rows; records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/position2-native-rows.out; records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/expression-check.out): at the rows read at once the merge rebuilt from the input as recorded lay 2.5e-4 in direction from the engine's own output, and with the input rounded as the engine rounds it 1.8e-7; at the later steps rounding would add an error instead of removing one. On the original file at all 70 matrices the old form leaves 21 parts in nine matrices past the bounds made from it (up to 680 times) and the corrected form none (at most 0.06 of a bound). The first sweep of the controlled training (controlled-bf16-1) took its target, its patterns and part of a floor from rows in the old form: a solve that was inside every bound was read by the engine four parts past theirs at the answers' first place. The solver was corrected in commit 7fec4404. The overlap it is aimed at, and the reference made from it, were still in the old form.
why_this_direction: Astra's decision of November 11 (records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-native-reference-decision-astra.md): the next sweep from the original file gets a fresh original-only reference with a matrix's input taken as the engine multiplied it, and the reference checks that its gap and chance are the declared state overlap's, so the overlap has to be recorded in the same form first, as a result of its own, with the first one preserved. This is step 3 of the method on the same recordings, the same 60 answers, the same registration and the same formulas: it corrects which computation the overlap measures, and changes no step of the method, no cohort and no formula. It is the next step because the sweep that follows cannot be declared on a target in one form and a solver in another: that mismatch is what the last sweep's engine reading showed. Nothing is read through the model for this: the rows are input-overlap's, as recorded while the original model generated.
repeating_pattern_check: What has repeated: a quantity the work stood on was not what the engine does. Twice in the controlled training the yardstick was something other than the engine's own output of the original BF16 file (a float32 copy of the model; the merge rebuilt from a matrix's input as recorded), and each time it was found only after a sweep or a solve had been built on it. This overlap is the third place the same form sat, found this time before the next sweep is declared. Why it keeps happening: the rebuilt merge was checked against the engine at steps decoded one at a time, where the two agree, and the rows read at once were assumed to behave the same. How this run tests it and does not assume it: the corrected form is the one that reproduces the engine's own output of the original file at every matrix (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/expression-check.out), and beside the new overlap this run records, cell by cell against the first one, everything that changed, rises and falls alike, and whether any cell changes side of gap > 2 chance. An older, different repetition is in state-overlap's declaration (an edit aimed at a quantity that looked like the discrepancy): this run does not touch that question; the discrepancy stays the gap of the states.

rule.members: The 60 answers of the registered correspondence, 30 that subtract the descent and 30 correct, in its order. Their rows are input-overlap's: what arrived at each of the 70 matrices and the state it added to, at every generated step, while the original model generated each answer token by token.
rule.state: For each matrix and step, the direction of the state right after the merge: unit(h + g*y/rms(y)), with y the matrix output for the recorded input as the engine multiplied it, g the learned scale after it and h the recorded state it is added to, computed with the original weights. As the engine multiplied it: at each answer's first step the input is rounded to the file's BF16 (round to nearest even on the float32 bits, tube.bf16), and at every later step it is as recorded (tube.multiplied, read as generated). Nothing else differs from state-overlap.
rule.overlap: As in the registered overlap of the turns, with its pairs: at a place, the mean of each answer's steps laid on that place, then the mean over the answers of each group. Per place and matrix: the squared gap of the two group means; its chance, the sum over the two groups of the answers' spread divided by their count; how alike the gaps of the two alternating halves are; the shared part, max(0, 1 - chance/gap).
rule.beside_it: Per place and matrix, what the shared turn gaps of the registered overlap (shared part where gap > 2 chance, at the 70 matrix merges) add up to along the path to that matrix, and what they would leave of the state gap if each were delivered in full: as a2-path first declared them, and with the first merge taken as the state after it. And the gap and chance of the direction of the token embeddings.
rule.against_the_first: Beside the overlap, deciding nothing (against-state-overlap.json): per matrix and over all, the cells (place, matrix) whose gap, chance or pattern differ from state-overlap's, how many rose and how many fell, the largest change either way, the cells that are diverged (gap > 2 chance) in one overlap and not in the other, both ways, and the places that hold an answer's first step. No value is chosen between the two overlaps: the new one is what the corrected computation gives (Astra: no minimum or maximum of old and new).

prediction.expected_observation: Only the 60 first steps of the 60 answers are computed differently, so only the places of the axis that hold a first step can change, in both patterns, the gap and the chance, at every matrix; at every other place the overlap is state-overlap's to the last digits, and so are the summaries over places 142 to 313 (gap 4.8 to 9.3 times chance, median 5.7). At the places that do change the patterns are expected to move by about the size of the correction over the steps laid there (2.5e-4 in direction at one step of the changed model's reading, 7e-5 to 7e-4 on the original file), which is small against most gaps but not against the smallest chances at the opening places, where the answers of a group hardly differ (1e-9 to 5e-6 in direction). Which way the gap and the chance move there is not predicted, and it can differ from matrix to matrix (Astra: the covariance of the correction with the state can have either sign). Whether any cell changes side of gap > 2 chance is not predicted either; if any does, it is at those places.
prediction.failures_only: Every cell that is diverged in one overlap and not in the other is listed with both values; so is any place that holds no first step and changed.

would_weaken_it: The hypothesis is not tested by this run: it expresses step 3 again on the same recordings. What it can show wrong is the correction as declared. If a place that holds no first step changed, the code reads the rows another way than this declaration says, and the result is not the same method. If the gap over places 142 to 313 moved at all, the same. If many cells at the opening places changed side of gap > 2 chance, the asked region there would rest on the engine's rounding and not on the answers, which would be reported to Astra before any sweep is aimed at those cells.
